target: Jag förstår dig.
english: I understand you.
tip: This verb takes -er in present tense (group 2), not -ar. Group 2 verbs are also very common in Swedish.

target: Jag gillar kaffe.
english: I like coffee.
tip: Group 1 verbs (-ar) are the largest and most regular group: 'talar, talade, talat'. New loan words almost always join this group.

target: Jag heter Erik.
english: My name is Erik.
tip: This verb takes -er in present (group 2). Past tense adds -de or -te depending on the stem consonant.

target: Han läser tidningen.
english: He reads the newspaper.
tip: 'Läsa' → 'läser' (read): Group 2 verb with -er present ending.

target: Hon somnar direkt.
english: She falls asleep right away.
tip: Swedish present tense is the same for all persons: `jag talar`, `du talar`, `han talar`. The verb form never changes by person. Easy compared to most European languages.

target: Vi bor i närheten.
english: We live nearby.
tip: Swedish word order: the verb is always in second position in declarative main clauses (V2 rule).

target: Hon undervisar i matematik.
english: She teaches mathematics.
tip: Swedish verbs don't change with person: 'jag talar', 'du talar', 'han talar' – same form for everyone.

target: Vi njöt av solnedgången.
english: We enjoyed the sunset.
tip: Swedish glues "the" onto the end of the noun. hund (a dog) → hunden (the dog). hus (a house) → huset (the house). No separate word.

target: Jag bor i Stockholm.
english: I live in Stockholm.
tip: 'Bo' → 'bor' (live): Group 3 verb – short infinitive, add -r for present.

target: Jag kommer från Sverige.
english: I am from Sweden.
tip: 'Komma' → 'kommer' (come): Group 4 irregular – the doubled -m- marks it.

target: Vi lagar middag tillsammans.
english: We cook dinner together.
tip: This is a group 1 (-ar) verb – the largest and most regular verb group in Swedish.

target: Det kostar tjugofem kronor.
english: It costs twenty-five kronor.
tip: Swedish numbers 21-99 put the tens first: tjugofem = twenty-five. No hyphen needed.

target: Jag dricker hellre te.
english: I'd rather drink tea.
tip: Endings tell you the verb group: -ar (group 1, regular), -er (group 2), -r on stems ending in vowel (group 3), zero (group 4 irregular). But the present form stays the same for every subject.

target: Han kör till kontoret.
english: He drives to the office.
tip: Swedish glues "the" onto the end of the noun. hund (a dog) → hunden (the dog). hus (a house) → huset (the house). No separate word.

target: De pratar svenska hemma.
english: They speak Swedish at home.
tip: 'Prata' → 'pratar' (talk/chat): Group 1, more informal than 'tala'.

target: Butiken öppnar klockan tio.
english: The store opens at ten.
tip: Two genders – common (suffix -n) and neuter (suffix -t). bilen (the car, common) vs huset (the house, neuter). The ending reveals the gender.

target: Det är min första dag.
english: It is my first day.
tip: "Första" = first. Ordinals 1-3 are irregular: första, andra, tredje.

target: Vi handlar mat varje vecka.
english: We buy food every week.
tip: Swedish present tense is formed by adding -r to the infinitive stem. It stays the same for all persons.

target: Jag äter frukost klockan sju.
english: I eat breakfast at seven.
tip: Swedish present tense: regular verbs simply add -r. The form is the same for all subjects.

target: De äter köttbullar till lunch.
english: They eat meatballs for lunch.
tip: Strong verbs (group 4) are common in everyday Swedish: 'gå/gick' (go/went), 'se/såg' (see/saw), 'ta/tog' (take/took).

target: Jag dricker kaffe varje morgon.
english: I drink coffee every morning.
tip: If you're unsure of a verb's group, the infinitive ending helps: -a with present -ar = group 1; -a with present -er = group 2.

target: Han jobbar på ett sjukhus.
english: He works at a hospital.
tip: 'Jobba' → 'jobbar' (work): Group 1 verb (-ar ending). 'Arbeta' → 'arbetar' is more formal.

target: Jag tvättar kläder varannan dag.
english: I do laundry every other day.
tip: Swedish object pronouns: 'mig' (me), 'dig' (you), 'honom' (him), 'henne' (her), 'oss' (us), 'dem' (them).

target: Jag tar bussen till skolan.
english: I take the bus to school.
tip: Swedish present tense: add -r to the stem. Group 1 gives -ar, groups 2-3 give -er/-r.

target: Vi dricker lättöl till maten.
english: We drink light beer with the food.
tip: "Lättöl" (light beer under 2.25%) can be sold in supermarkets, unlike stronger beers.

target: Jag arbetar på ett stort kontor.
english: I work at a large office.
tip: Swedish present tense adds "-r" to the infinitive: "talar" (speak/speaks).

target: Vi tycker att filmen var bra.
english: We think the movie was good.
tip: Irregular verbs like 'vara' (be), 'ha' (have), and 'göra' (do) don't fit neatly into groups – memorize their forms individually.

target: Jag sover åtta timmar varje natt.
english: I sleep eight hours every night.
tip: Winter tires are legally required in Sweden from December 1 to March 31.

target: Vi möter våra vänner på lördag.
english: We meet our friends on Saturday.
tip: Group 2 verbs split into 2a (-er, past -de) and 2b (-er, past -te). The consonant before the ending determines which subgroup.

target: Jag dricker alltid kaffe till frukosten.
english: I always drink coffee with breakfast.
tip: This is a strong (group 4) verb – it changes its stem vowel in past tense rather than adding a suffix.

target: Han ringde henne igår i affären.
english: He called her yesterday in the store.
tip: Object pronouns: mig, dig, honom, henne, oss, er, dem. "Henne" = her (object).

target: Vi äter frukost klockan halv åtta.
english: We eat breakfast at half past seven.
tip: "Halv åtta" = 7:30 (half TO eight). "Frukost" = breakfast.

target: Vi behöver byta tåg i Nässjö.
english: We need to change trains in Nässjö.
tip: "Byta tåg" = change trains. Nässjö is a major rail junction.

target: Vi äter lunch klockan halv ett.
english: We eat lunch at half past twelve.
tip: "Vem" = who, "Vad" = what, "Var" = where, "När" = when, "Hur" = how.

target: Hon är duktig på att laga mat.
english: She is good at cooking.
tip: "Duktig på" = good at – very common in Swedish.

target: Javisst, det kan jag hjälpa dig med.
english: Certainly, I can help you with that.
tip: "Javisst" combines "ja" and "visst" (certainly). Very emphatic agreement.

target: De bor i ett stort hus här.
english: They live in a big house here.
tip: "Bo" is Group 3: bor (present), bodde (past), bott (supine). Short and common.

target: Jag har en bror och en syster.
english: I have a brother and a sister.
tip: 'Har' (have/has) – same form for all persons. Used for possession and as perfect tense auxiliary.

target: Det borde gå bra just nu också.
english: It should be fine right now too.
tip: Past endings: -ade (group 1, most regular), -de or -te (group 2). tittade (looked), läste (read), köpte (bought). Same form for every subject.

target: Bussen stannar vid torget.
english: The bus stops at the square.
tip: "Torget" = the square/marketplace. "Vid" = at/by (for locations near something).

target: Det är den femtonde mars.
english: It is the fifteenth of March.
tip: Ordinal dates use -e or -te endings: femtonde = fifteenth. Swedish dates go day-month.

target: Vi äter middag klockan sex.
english: We eat dinner at six o'clock.
tip: "Middag" = dinner (evening meal). Lunch is the midday meal.

target: Han lämnar barnen på dagis.
english: He drops the children off at daycare.
tip: Dagis (daycare) is widely available and affordable in Sweden.

target: Jag åker Öresundståget till Köpenhamn.
english: I take the Öresund train to Copenhagen.
tip: The Öresund Bridge connects Sweden to Denmark – a twenty-minute train ride.

target: Jag vill lära mig mer svenska.
english: I want to learn more Swedish.
tip: 'Vill' (want) – modal verbs in Swedish don't change form: 'jag vill', 'du vill', 'han vill'.

target: I morse åt vi frukost tidigt.
english: This morning we ate breakfast early.
tip: "I morse" = this morning. Past tense because the morning has passed.

target: Han skriver långa mejl till sin chef.
english: He writes long emails to his boss.
tip: 'Skriva' → 'skriver' (write): Group 4 strong verb – the -er ending is typical.

target: Mannen som bor här är min granne.
english: The man who lives here is my neighbor.
tip: "Som" is the all-purpose relative pronoun – it replaces who, which, that.

target: Flickan som sjunger har en fin röst.
english: The girl who sings has a beautiful voice.
tip: "Som" is the universal relative pronoun in spoken Swedish – works for who, which, that.

target: Barnet som leker i parken är glatt.
english: The child playing in the park is happy.
tip: "Som" never changes form – same for subjects, objects, en/ett/plural. Universal relative pronoun.

target: Jag heter Erik och jag lär mig svenska.
english: My name is Erik and I'm learning Swedish.
tip: 'Jag är' (I am) – Swedish present tense of 'vara' (to be) is 'är' for all persons.

target: Han springer fem kilometer varje morgon innan frukost.
english: He runs five kilometers every morning before breakfast.
tip: This is a strong (group 4) verb – it changes its stem vowel in past tense: present -er, past has vowel change.

target: I Sverige äter man ofta middag vid sex.
english: In Sweden one often eats dinner at six.
tip: Swedish is V2: the verb is always the second element. `Idag äter jag pizza` (today I eat pizza), not `idag jag äter`. Subject jumps after the verb.

target: Jag arbetar hemifrån tre dagar i veckan numera.
english: I work from home three days a week nowadays.
tip: Swedish present tense adds -r. Group 1 verbs add -ar, group 2 add -er.

target: De studerar ekonomi vid Lunds universitet sedan hösten.
english: They have been studying economics at Lund University since autumn.
tip: 'Studera' → 'studerar' (study): Group 1 verb with -ar present ending.

target: Jag har precis börjat lära mig svenska på kvällskurs.
english: I have just started learning Swedish in evening class.
tip: 'Har' (have) is the same for all persons in Swedish: 'jag har', 'du har', 'vi har'.

target: Vi planterar blommor och grönsaker i trädgården varje vår.
english: We plant flowers and vegetables in the garden every spring.
tip: 'Vi' (we) – Swedish pronouns: jag, du, han/hon/den/det, vi, ni, de (pronounced 'dom').

target: Jag förstår inte vad du menar med den frågan.
english: I do not understand what you mean with that question.
tip: Swedish present tense: add -r to the infinitive stem. Same form for all persons: jag/du/han/vi all use '-r'.

target: Hej, jag heter Anna och jag kommer från Stockholm.
english: Hello, my name is Anna and I come from Stockholm.
tip: Swedish present tense: all persons share the same verb form ending in -r.

target: Hon bakar bröd varje helg och delar med grannarna.
english: She bakes bread every weekend and shares with the neighbors.
tip: Most verbs you'll encounter daily are group 1 (-ar) – recognizing this pattern speeds up comprehension significantly.
